pages.text: "I know this! It is for eating!" Gaga, who knew best, plucked a red berry. Red berries hung in clusters on a bush beside the pebble shore. Gaga stretched their neck and held it up.
"I found it first, so everyone ask me." Careless Duri came to look. "What berry is that?" Gaga hid it tightly in a closed hand.
Teacher Bau sat on the pebbles, watching the children. Gaga glanced that way, then turned away. "No need to ask. I know everything."
Gaga brought the berry to their mouth. Startled, Duri caught their hand. "No! You do not know what it is!" Gaga's hand stopped right before the mouth.
Duri spread a palm wide. "Unfamiliar berries? Show Teacher first!" "No. I told you I know it!" Gaga squeezed tighter.
The berry burst in that tight hand. Red juice ran between the fingers. "Oh... oh?" Gaga opened their hand, and the berry was gone.
There was no berry to show or boast about. Gaga's hands were sticky and red. Washing by the water kept Gaga from playing with pebbles.
Teacher Bau dried Gaga's hands with a towel. "Put unfamiliar things on your palm, so everyone can see." Teacher Bau opened a big palm wide.
A little later, Gaga found a yellow berry in the bush. "One, do not put it in my mouth! Two, place it on my palm! Three, show Teacher first!" Gaga ran with an open palm, purple ribbon fluttering.

Teacher Bau looked closely. "This berry is not for eating. Gaga found it first!" Teacher Bau hugged Gaga's shoulders. Unfamiliar things go on a palm, not in a mouth. "Duri, see? Unfamiliar berries? Show Teacher first!"
